protocol:
MEOS-0, sixth stage, follow-up: the three actions the main Stage 6 experiments could not build (coupling.bypass, resource.rerouting, address.temporary_local; engine meos-0.5).

Same protocol as Pipeline A and B, with the same criterion (``stage6_experiments.row_ok``), on the same stresses, tick grid and seed sets (exploration 1-5, validation 6-10, evaluation 11-30; a setting is validated only if it is effective on all five
validation seeds; 3-4 of 5 is a near miss and is kept). Nothing of the frozen Stage 6 results is changed: this adds rows to the tested action space and the classification is reported twice, with the original action space and with the extended one.
A combined repair counts as a combined recovery only where neither of its two parts is effective alone (the Stage 6 rule), the new action being one part.

actions.label: bypass of the damaged coupling: a second path for A1's alteration to reach A2
actions.magnitude_meaning: share of the peak of A1's own sensing window that reaches A2 (absent = 0)
actions.side_effect: A2 can fire on A1's alteration without the coupling; it can also fire when the damaged coupling would have kept it silent
actions.note: engine meos-0.5: A2's stimulus is max(gain x peak of its window, bypass x peak of A1's window); the coupling itself stays damaged

actions.label: transport rerouting: a conduit from the source edge of the resource gradient to A1's cell, for a duration
actions.magnitude_meaning: share of the source cell moved to A1's cell per tick
actions.side_effect: the source cell (0, 6) is drained while the conduit runs
actions.reversibility: reversible by construction (the conduit ends); the moved resource stays
actions.note: engine meos-0.5: resource is moved from (0, 6) to (3, 6) each tick; the total is conserved by the conduit itself

actions.label: temporary local addressing: A2 is fully addressable for a duration, then its address state returns
actions.side_effect: the degraded Address returns when the duration ends
actions.note: engine meos-0.5: ADDRESS mode temporary; a later address intervention ends it at once
